intended_object: The classical inhomogeneous-to-homogeneous passage of continuous cochains in degree 1 for trivial 𝔽₂ coefficients: a continuous f : G → ℤ/2 is sent to the homogeneous 1-cochain (g₀, g₁) ↦ f(g₀⁻¹g₁). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation (citing Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Ch. I §2) and the name.
explanation: The body curries the jointly continuous map (g₀, g₁) ↦ (trivialF2Equiv G).symm (f (g₀⁻¹ * g₁)). The symm step only moves the value into the lifted carrier ULift (ZMod 2) of trivialF2 G. Continuity follows from the continuity of f, multiplication and inversion. The proof obligation is invariance under the diagonal action, which defines homogeneousCochains; with the trivial action it reduces to (g⁻¹h₀)⁻¹(g⁻¹h₁) = h₀⁻¹h₁, which the simp proof checks. The general homogeneous form g₀ • f(g₀⁻¹g₁) (the library's homogeneous1) agrees with f(g₀⁻¹g₁) because the action is trivial. Lemmas in the same file confirm the intent: the image is a cocycle exactly when f is additive, and its differential is the image of the inhomogeneous coboundary (g, h) ↦ ψ h − ψ(gh) + ψ g. The passage makes sense for any discrete module, and the library already provides that general version as TauCeti.ContCohomology.cochainEquiv1. This constructor is a deliberate 𝔽₂ specialisation: it takes ZMod 2-valued functions and handles the crossing into the universe-lifted carrier of trivialF2 G, which only makes sense for this coefficient module, so it is not too narrow. I found no Mathlib counterpart: Mathlib has no homogeneousCochains (the complex used here comes from the library), and no continuous-cohomology inhomogeneous-to-homogeneous map turned up in my searches.
